_comment: Pinned inventory of every third-party (and locally built) asset that the Flutter *web*
bundle ships out of web/. It is the single source of truth for tool/fetch_web_deps.py and
for the license disclosure -- the web-side counterpart of the *_URL / *_SHA256 constants in
tool/fetch_deps.py, which pin the Windows native prebuilts.
Entries are keyed by the file's path relative to web/. Fields:
sha256       -- SHA-256 of the exact bytes that must land on disk.
bytes        -- size of those bytes, as a cheap second check and a review aid.
origin       -- 'upstream' (fetchable and hash-verifiable) or 'in-tree' (produced here;
no byte-level upstream claim is possible, so 'build' records provenance).
build.sources-- (in-tree only) a digest of the sources the artifact was built from, plus
the selection that produced it. Every other field here compares bytes to
their pin, which cannot see the one failure that matters for a locally
built, gitignored artifact: the bytes still match while the C++ they came
from has moved on. This block makes that comparable, and it needs neither
emsdk nor the artifact on disk, so CI checks it too. Line endings are
normalised to LF before hashing, so a CRLF checkout and a Linux runner
agree. The selection over-approximates on purpose (every header under the
roots, not the module's real include closure): a false 'stale' costs a
rebuild, a false 'fresh' would ship the wrong binary. 'exclude' mirrors
native/wasm/build.sh's EXCLUDED_SOURCES, and check_sources.py holds the
two together. What it proves is 'the recorded digest equals this tree',
and no more: nothing reads the binary back, so repinning without
rebuilding passes. It removes the SILENT failure, where the manifest is
never touched and the stale pin verifies against its own bytes.
upstream     -- url / package / version of the artifact the bytes come from. When the
artifact is an archive, 'member' names the path inside it; without
'member' the url is the file itself.
license      -- SPDX-ish id plus 'asset', a repo-relative path to the committed text.
Optional 'parent' marks the text as a *sub-notice* of an already
disclosed package (e.g. fmt inside spdlog): the license page shows it
under that package instead of inventing a separate dependency entry.
source_form  -- how to obtain the corresponding sources: 'url' + 'sha256' pin an
immutable source archive, and 'git_url' points at the upstream tag or
commit. No self-hosted mirror is kept.
Everything under web/wasm/ is gitignored and provisioned locally; web/coi-serviceworker.js
is committed. Both are listed here, so the manifest also doubles as the answer to 'what
exactly does this repo place under web/, and under which license'. It does NOT cover the
rest of build/web/: Flutter emits flutter.js, flutter_bootstrap.js, main.dart.js and the
CanvasKit / Skwasm payload at build time, and those carry the Flutter SDK's own licensing.
'first_party' below lists this repo's own hand-written files under web/ (verified against
'git ls-files web/'). Anything under web/ that is neither pinned in 'files' nor allow-listed
there is flagged by tool/fetch_web_deps.py, because 'flutter build web' would publish it.
To bump an upstream dependency:
1. Pick the new version and download its artifact once (npm tarball or raw release file).
2. sha256sum the artifact and each shipped member, and record the byte sizes.
3. Update this entry's sha256 / bytes / upstream.version / upstream.url and the matching
source_form.url + source_form.sha256 + source_form.git_url.
4. Refresh license.asset under assets/license/ if the upstream license text changed.
5. Run: uv run tool/fetch_web_deps.py --force --only <package>
It re-downloads, verifies every hash against this file, and fails loudly on a mismatch.
To refresh an in-tree entry, rebuild it (native/wasm/build.sh), copy the artifacts into
web/wasm/, then update sha256 / bytes / build.* here -- including build.sources.digest,
which 'dart run tool/check_web_pins.dart --source-digest' prints. Repinning the bytes and
leaving the digest behind is itself a failure, so the two cannot drift apart silently.
'uv run tool/fetch_web_deps.py' reports in-tree drift as a warning rather than
re-downloading anything.
WHO FAILS ON A STALE build.sources.digest: CI and tool/build_web.sh, i.e. everything that
decides what ships. tool/hooks/pre-commit does NOT -- it passes
--warn-stale-source-digest, so it prints the drift and lets the commit through. Rebuilding
the module needs an emsdk toolchain, and a fatal check there would make every native/
change uncommittable from a machine that has none. Committing a native/ change with the
pin left behind is therefore allowed and expected; the rebuild+repin above is what clears
the CI failure before the branch can merge.
'provisioned_root' is the gitignored prefix (see .gitignore) that has to be provisioned
before a web build. When nothing under it exists, the tree is simply un-provisioned --
an ordinary Windows-only checkout -- and DistributionInfoBuilder emits
assets/web_license_info.json with status 'not_provisioned' instead of failing. That only
changes the status: the pins and the closed-world scan still run over whatever IS on disk,
so the committed half of web/ (coi-serviceworker.js) is verified in every checkout.
This repo's own hand-written files under web/ -- everything 'git ls-files web/' reports
except coi-serviceworker.js, which is third-party and therefore pinned in 'files' instead.
Paths are relative to web/ and match EXACTLY: there is deliberately no directory-prefix
form, because a prefix would allow an unbounded number of unreviewed files underneath it.
Adding a hand-written file under web/ therefore means adding it here (and a third-party
one means pinning it in 'files'), otherwise codegen refuses to emit the disclosure.
Symbolic links are never first-party, whatever they are named.

source_form.note: The upstream repository carries no git tags, so the source form is pinned to the 'Prepare v0.1.7 release' commit; the file at that commit is byte-identical to the npm 0.1.7 tarball's coi-serviceworker.js. This is a single hand-written file, so the shipped bytes are already the source form.

This prebuilt .wasm statically links the ONNX Runtime C++ core and its own third-party dependencies. Its component licenses are the ones ONNX Runtime discloses for the v1.27.0 tag; only the top-level MIT text is reproduced here.

MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: it is accepted for this web-only asset because the bundle is shipped unmodified and hash-pinned, and the source form above discloses the exact sources. The bundle carries no version string, so the version is established by the npm tarball's own digest rather than by reading the file. The pub-side reject list in lib/distribution_info.dart is unaffected -- mediabunny is not a pub package.
Shipped next to the bundle so the MPL-2.0 notice travels with the code it covers. Byte-identical to assets/license/mediabunny.txt.

build.git_commit_note: git_commit is null on purpose, not left blank by oversight: no commit reproduces these bytes on its own. This module was rebuilt 2026-08-28 against the UNCOMMITTED working tree of fix/test-harness-and-wasm-toolchain, to clear the build.sources.digest staleness that comment-only edits under native/src and native/wasm/build.sh (stale path citations corrected in prose) had introduced; the edits, these artifacts and this repin land together in one commit that did not exist when the build ran. Even once it exists it is internal to a branch that has never been pushed, so a squash or rebase merge into develop would orphan it -- which is exactly what the previous value, 9bca991b, already was, and it was additionally one commit older than the misc.h state it described. build.sources.digest is the durable identity here: it is content-addressed over native/src, native/vendor and native/wasm with line endings normalised, so it survives any history rewrite, and it is the field the checks actually compare (nothing reads git_commit). Name a commit here again only once one exists that reproduces these bytes by itself -- i.e. after this branch lands on develop. EVIDENCE OF AN ACTUAL REBUILD: build.sh recompiles unconditionally (no incremental skip), and this run compiled all 11 translation units and linked once in 130 s; the 11 obj/*.o mtimes and both outputs fall in a single window 00:47:05-00:48:48 on 2026-08-28, strictly after the invocation started. RESULT: both artifacts came out BYTE-IDENTICAL to the previous pin (umacapture_core.js sha256 57693fa4..., 125370 bytes; umacapture_core.wasm sha256 3befc2ce..., 3622922 bytes). That is the expected outcome, not a skipped build: every changed line under the digest roots is a comment, and the toolchain paths that bake into the module via __FILE__ did not move this time. So sha256 and bytes are unchanged and only build.sources.digest moved, 52a52a24... -> aac99172.... Toolchain unchanged at its C:/Projects/umacapture-wasm-toolchain defaults for EMSDK_DIR/OPENCV_DIR/BUILD_DIR.

source_form.note: Emscripten JS loader glue emitted alongside umacapture_core.wasm. Its third-party content is the Emscripten runtime support code; see the 'linked' list on the .wasm entry.

linked.name: OpenCV
linked.evidence: native/wasm/build.sh OPENCV_LIBS; the module's embedded cv::getBuildInformation() string reports 'OpenCV 4.13.0'.

linked.name: OpenCV core: softfloat (Berkeley SoftFloat 3c and FDLIBM derived)
linked.evidence: modules/core/src/softfloat.cpp carries its own notices on top of OpenCV's Apache-2.0 text, which does not reproduce them. softfloat.cpp.o is present in libopencv_core.a (llvm-ar t), and the module contains cv::softfloat assert strings such as 'softfloat((int)LAB_CBRT_TAB_SIZE)'.

linked.name: libpng
linked.evidence: Linked via liblibpng.a in build.sh; the embedded OpenCV build string reports 'PNG: build (ver 1.6.53)' and the module contains libpng's own error strings.

linked.name: libjpeg-turbo
linked.evidence: Linked via liblibjpeg-turbo.a in build.sh; the embedded OpenCV build string reports 'JPEG: build-libjpeg-turbo (ver 3.1.2-70)'.

linked.name: zlib
linked.evidence: Linked via libzlib.a in build.sh; the embedded OpenCV build string reports 'ZLib: build (ver 1.3.1)'.

linked.name: Emscripten runtime (libc syscalls, pthread, embind)
linked.evidence: em++ links these implicitly (-pthread, -lembind); the module's source-path strings include 'emscripten/system/lib/pthread/*.c'.

linked.name: LLVM runtimes: libc++, libc++abi, compiler-rt
linked.evidence: -fexceptions plus C++ standard-library use; the module's source-path strings include 'libcxxabi/src/cxa_exception_emscripten.cpp', 'cxa_demangle.cpp' and 'private_typeinfo.cpp'.

linked.name: spdlog
linked.evidence: Header-only vendored dependency of native/src/util/logger_util.*; the module contains mangled spdlog:: symbols.

linked.name: {fmt} (bundled inside the vendored spdlog snapshot)

license.id: MIT (plus fmt's optional embedding exception; no registered SPDX id)

linked.evidence: native/vendor/spdlog/VENDORED.md records that spdlog 1.17.0 bundles {fmt} 12.1.0 (fmt/bundled/base.h: FMT_VERSION 120100). SPDLOG_FMT_EXTERNAL is not defined, so spdlog/fmt/fmt.h takes the bundled path and the include closure pulls in the fmt/bundled/* headers; the module contains 'N3fmt3v1212format_errorE' and 'N3fmt3v1212format_facet' mangled symbols. Disclosed separately from spdlog because assets/license/spdlog.txt only links to fmt's licence by URL, and fmt's text adds an 'Optional exception' clause that spdlog's MIT does not carry.

linked.name: nlohmann/json
linked.evidence: Header-only vendored dependency of native/src/util/json_util.h; the module contains 'nlohmann::json_abi_v3_12_0' mangled symbols.

linked.name: eventpp
linked.evidence: Header-only vendored dependency of native/src/util/event_util.h; the module contains 'eventpp::internal_::CallbackList' mangled symbols.

linked.name: nameof
linked.evidence: Header-only vendored dependency of native/src/condition/basic_condition.h, which is in the wasm translation units' include closure. Its output is compile-time string literals, so it leaves no mangled symbols.

linked.name: minimal_uuid4
linked.evidence: Header-only vendored dependency of native/src/chara_detail/chara_detail_scene_scraper.h, which is compiled into the module.

source_form.note: Built here from native/src + native/wasm, so no byte-level upstream claim is made. CLI11, doctest and FFmpeg are NOT part of this module -- they belong to the CLI and test targets only, which native/wasm/build.sh does not compile.
